'''Daniel Alva Griffith''' (born November 15, 1948) is an American geographer, spatial statistician, and geographic information scientist (GIScientist). He is known for his contributions to quantitative geography and spatial statistics, particularly for developing the Moran eigenvector spatial filtering (MESF) technique and introducing the sui-random variables model, both of which address spatial autocorrelation in regression modeling.<ref>{{cite book |last=Griffith |first=Daniel A. |title=Spatial Autocorrelation and Spatial Filtering: Gaining Understanding Through Theory and Scientific Visualization |publisher=Springer |year=2003 |doi=10.1007/978-3-540-24806-4 |isbn=9783540248064}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Griffith |first1=Daniel A. |last2=Anselin |first2=Luc |title=Do spatial effects really matter in regression analysis? |journal=Papers of the Regional Science Association |volume=65 |issue=1 |year=1988 |pages=11–34 |doi=10.1111/j.1435-5597.1988.tb01155.x}}</ref> His work has applications in geography, economics, epidemiology, environmental sciences, and other disciplines.

Griffith is Ashbel Smith Professor Emeritus of Geospatial Information Sciences at the [[University of Texas at Dallas]].<ref name="UTDprofile">{{cite web |title=Daniel A. Griffith – UT Dallas profile |url=https://profiles.utdallas.edu/dagriffith |website=University of Texas at Dallas |access-date=10 September 2025}}</ref> Since 2021, bibliometric rankings such as Research.com and ScholarGPS have placed him among the top 0.05% of global scholars in geography, with one ranking listing him as the top spatial analyst worldwide.<ref>{{cite web |title=Daniel A. Griffith – Research.com profile |url=https://research.com/u/daniel-a-griffith |website=Research.com |access-date=10 September 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Daniel A. Griffith – ScholarGPS profile |url=https://scholargps.com/scholars/70553017924539/daniel-a-griffith |access-date=10 September 2025 |website=ScholarGPS}}</ref>

== Early life and education ==
Griffith was born in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, and raised in Westmoreland County. He earned a B.S. in mathematics education and an M.A. in geography from [[Indiana University of Pennsylvania]].<ref>{{cite book |last=Griffith |first=Daniel A. |title=Becoming a Geographer in the Shadow of Geography's Quantitative Revolution |publisher=Routledge |year=2025 |editor=Cox, Kevin |chapter=Geographical Journeys: Geographers Tell Their Stories |pages=162–175}}</ref> He completed a Ph.D. in geography at the [[University of Toronto]], followed by an M.S. in statistics at [[Pennsylvania State University]].<ref name="UTDprofile" />

== Academic career ==
Griffith has held faculty positions at [[Toronto Metropolitan University]], the [[University at Buffalo]], [[Syracuse University]], the [[University of Miami]], and the [[University of Texas at Dallas]], where he was Ashbel Smith Professor and later became professor emeritus.<ref name="UTDprofile" /> He also held courtesy appointments at [[SUNY College of Environmental Science and Forestry]], the [[University of Alberta]], and the [[University of Central Florida]].

He has been a visiting scholar at institutions including the [[University of Cambridge]], the [[Max Planck Institute for Demographic Research]], and [[Wuhan University]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Daniel A. Griffith visiting positions |url=https://loop.frontiersin.org/people/1352125/overview |website=Frontiers |access-date=10 September 2025}}</ref>

From 2008 to 2014 he served as editor of ''[[Geographical Analysis (journal)|Geographical Analysis]]''.<ref>{{cite news |title=Professor to edit leading geospatial journal |url=https://news.utdallas.edu/faculty-staff/professor-to-edit-leading-geospatial-journal/ |work=UT Dallas News |date=28 May 2008 |access-date=10 September 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Editorship of Geographical Analysis |url=https://regionalscience.org/index.php/news/miscellaneous-news/item/1056-editorship-of-geographical-analysis.html |website=Regional Science Association International |date=5 August 2013 |access-date=10 September 2025}}</ref>

== Research and contributions ==
Griffith’s research focuses on methods to address [[spatial autocorrelation]], a statistical phenomenon in which nearby values are correlated more than expected by chance. His development of the Moran eigenvector spatial filtering (MESF) approach has been widely cited and applied …<ref name="Book2003">{{cite book |last=Griffith |first=Daniel A. |title=Spatial Autocorrelation and Spatial Filtering: Gaining Understanding Through Theory and Scientific Visualization |year=2003 |publisher=Springer |isbn=9783540248064 |doi=10.1007/978-3-540-24806-4}}</ref> He also introduced the sui-random variables model as a framework for handling self-correlated data.<ref>{{cite journal |last=Griffith |first=Daniel A. |year=2025 |title=Beyond auto-models: self-correlated sui-model respecifications |url=https://doi.org/10.1111/gean.12411 |journal=Geographical Analysis |volume=57 |issue=1 |pages=127–151 |doi=10.1111/gean.12411|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

His methods have been implemented in [[R (programming language)|R]], MATLAB, SAS, and ArcGIS. Dedicated tools include ESFtool, a .NET-based regression tool,<ref>{{cite web |title=ESFtool |url=https://github.com/esftool/esftool |website=GitHub |access-date=10 September 2025}}</ref> and SAAR, an ArcGIS-integrated software with R.<ref>{{cite web |title=SAAR: Spatial Analysis using ArcGIS Engine and R |url=https://thesaar.github.io |access-date=10 September 2025}}</ref>

In applied work, Griffith’s spatial analyses of pediatric blood-lead levels in Syracuse, New York, using Onondaga County Health Department data, demonstrated neighborhood-level clustering of elevated lead exposure and contributed to public health research on lead-poisoning prevention and remediation.<ref>{{cite journal |last=Griffith |first=Daniel A. |year=1998 |title=A Tale of two swaths: urban childhood blood lead levels across Syracuse, NY |url=https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1111/0004-5608.00116 |journal=Annals of the Association of American Geographers |volume=30 |issue=3 |pages=640-665 |doi=10.1111/0004-5608.00116|url-access=subscription }}</ref>
